chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Khalid ibn Muhammad Al-Asamm, who said:

A man entered the Sacred Mosque while in Ihram, so he entered into Tawaf wearing a shirt and a robe. The people came upon him, tearing his shirt, and he was firm (did not remove it). Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saw them handling his shirt and tearing it, so he said to him, 'What did you do?' He said, 'I entered Ihram like this, with the shirt and robe on.' He said, 'Remove it from your head; it is not removed from your feet. Rather, it was ignorance.' Then someone else came to him and asked him, saying, 'What do you say about a man who enters Ihram with a shirt on?' He said, 'He should remove it from his head.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a man who enters Ihram wearing a shirt and robe?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (AS) corrects the common misconception that the shirt must be fully removed from the feet, clarifying that only the portion covering the head is removed while the lower part remains, as the prohibition specifically targets the head covering. This ruling highlights the distinction between the general prohibition of stitched garments and the specific requirements for Ihram attire, emphasizing that the garment's structure determines its permissibility rather than its complete removal. The incident underscores the practical application of fiqh principles in the context of Hajj rituals, where precision in ritual purity and attire is paramount.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Khalid Bin Muhammad Al Asamma who said,

‘A man entered the Sacred Masjid and he was in Ihraam. So he entered in the circumambulation and upon him was a shirt and a robe. So the people came upon him, tearing his shirt, and he was firm. So Abu Abdullahasws saw him, and they were handling his shirt, tearing it. So heasws said to him: ‘What did you do?’ So he said, ‘I wore it like this inside my shirt and my robe’. So heasws said: ‘Remove it from his head, not removing it from his leg. But rather it was ignorance’. So, someone else came to himasws and asked himasws saying, ‘So what are youasws saying regarding a man who wears Ihraam inside his shirt?’ Heasws said: ‘He should remove it from his head’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Khalid ibn Muhammad al-Asamm who has said the following:

“A man entered Masjid al-Haram in the state of Ihram and began performing Tawaf with a shirt and a gown on him. People went to him and tore his shirt, but he stood firm. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, saw him when people were tearing his shirt. He (the Imam) asked him about how he has done it. He said, ‘I assumed the state of Ihram like this in my shirt and gown.’ He (the Imam) told him to remove it from the direction of his head. ‘One like him is not required to remove it from the direction of his legs. He did not know (the rule).’ Another one came and asked him (the Imam), ‘What do you say about a man who assumes the state of Ihram in his shirt?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He must remove it from the direction of his head.’” (Fatwa best explains this Hadith)
